newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers want to raise prices--D&B.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers want to raise prices--D&B.

text.p: U.S. manufacturers expect their sector to grow at a much faster pace in the three months ahead, The Dun and Bradstreet Corp said on Thursday.
Dun and Bradstreet said its industrial sentiment index rose to 29 in January -- its highest level since it was created in 1990 -- versus 22 in December, 18 in November, and 20 a year ago.
Also, the D&B manufacturing production index shot up in January to a reading of 65 from 47 in December and 38 in November. That index stood at 45 in January 1996.
The new orders index was 66 in January versus 51 in December, 42 in November, and 48 a year ago.
Such optimistic expectations led manufacturers to expect to push prices higher in the three months ahead, D&B also reported in its survey of 1,000 manufacturing executives.
"The near-term future looks very bright to most manufacturers," said D&B chief economist Joseph Duncan.

"As they have for mot of the past year, manufacturers once again reported that they expect to increase prices over the coming months," added Duncan who noted similar expectations were not been followed by actual price increases last year.

"A solid majority of manufacturing executives expect to increase their production levels and sales during the coming months as high levels of employment and consumer confidence help sustain healthy economic performance," Duncan also said.
